subject: System Design
title: REST APIs
description: A quick, practical guide to REST APIs.

hook.text: Almost every app you use talks to servers through REST APIs. They're the lingua franca of the web.

buildup.text: REST uses HTTP verbs — GET, POST, PUT, DELETE — to perform operations on resources.

discovery.text: Each resource has a URL. GET /users/42 retrieves user 42. DELETE /users/42 removes them.

twist.text: REST is simple but can be chatty. Fetching a complex page might require dozens of separate API calls.

climax.text: REST's simplicity made it the default. Its limitations spawned GraphQL and gRPC.

punchline.text: Simple, universal, and good enough for most systems.

quiz.question: What HTTP verb retrieves a resource in REST?
